title: Private upgrade plan v1: generate staged, auditable upgrade plan in installer
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Context / Problem
Private upgrades today are too imperative and operator-dependent (run a few commands, hope ordering is right, discover incompatibilities mid-flight). This has led to upgrade-related incidents (e.g., DB migration lock contention, partial chart rollouts, artifact mismatches in air-gapped envs) and high support load.

This parent issue tracks the upgrade plan generation milestone: introduce a deterministic, versioned “upgrade plan” artifact that the installer can generate ahead of time, validate, and then execute with clear phase boundaries and rollback entry points.

Goals
- Safe-by-default, consistent upgrade workflow for Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem/air-gapped).
- Generate an upgrade plan with explicit stages, ordering, prerequisites, and rollback metadata.
- Operator-friendly UX: plan preview, actionable failures, and an auditable summary.
- Enable downstream work: prechecks framework, backup orchestration, rollback state machine, Helm ordering, and version gating.

Non-goals (v1)
- Fully automated multi-hop upgrades across many major versions (default path is N-1 → N).
- Solving every historical migration edge case automatically; v1 must clearly surface “manual intervention required” with pointers.

Definition of Done (v1)
1) Plan artifact
- Installer can generate a machine-readable plan file (JSON) with:
  - schema_version (plan schema)
  - environment metadata (install type: vpc|onprem, k8s version, storage class, registry/chart sources)
  - from_version / to_version (pinned)
  - ordered stages and steps with:
    - step_id, name, description
    - preconditions (refs to prechecks)
    - expected duration / timeout hints
    - rollback_strategy and rollback_step refs (where applicable)
    - artifacts required (images/charts/bundles, checksums if offline)
  - “operator notes” section for warnings + remediation pointers
- Plan is deterministic: same inputs → same plan (no hidden mutable state).

2) Installer UX
- CLI supports:
  - redwood-private upgrade plan --from <ver> --to <ver> [--output plan.json] [--offline-bundle <path>]
  - redwood-private upgrade plan --validate <plan.json>
  - redwood-private upgrade plan --summary <plan.json>
- Output includes an auditable human summary: phases, blocking requirements, warnings, and required artifacts.

3) Persistence / audit hooks (minimum viable)
- Plan output can be attached to support bundles and stored alongside upgrade state (implementation details tracked in ENG-4899).
- Emit at least one lifecycle marker/event in installer logs with plan_id / plan_hash for traceability (full audit log events tracked in platform work).

4) Integration points
- Plan stages align with Helm CP/DP separation (ENG-4860) and rollback entry points (ENG-4844).
- Plan generation blocks unsupported upgrade paths via compatibility policy (platform dependency; see redwood PR-29104).

5) Test coverage
- Unit tests for plan generation determinism and required fields.
- Integration test “happy path” (N-1 → N) in CI for VPC; on-prem/offline coverage can start as nightly (tracked in ENG-4877).

Proposed Plan Structure (high-level)
Stage 0: Inputs + compatibility gating
- Validate from/to versions, supported path (N-1 → N default)
- Validate artifact sources (online registries/chart repos OR offline bundle manifest)

Stage 1: Prechecks (blocking + warning)
- Cluster health, node readiness, control-plane connectivity
- Storage headroom (etcd + db PVCs + object store / PV snapshots)
- DB connectivity and migration prerequisites
- RBAC/SSO reachability (OIDC/SAML endpoints), TLS/DNS

Stage 2: Backup / snapshots (if enabled per policy)
- Trigger snapshot hooks / logical dumps depending on backend
- Verify backup integrity marker and record restore instructions

Stage 3: Control plane upgrade
- Upgrade installer-managed CP components first
- Gate on readiness + basic control-plane API checks

Stage 4: Migrations / config persistence updates
- Run schema migrations with guardrails (lock timeouts, idempotency)
- If migration requires manual intervention, plan must stop with explicit instructions

Stage 5: Data plane rollout
- Roll DP components after CP is healthy
- Gate on DP readiness and a minimal synthetic request

Stage 6: Postchecks + finalize
- Verify versions, health endpoints, reconcile drift
- Record completion summary and pointers to rollback command semantics

Rollout plan
- Phase A (internal): ship behind a feature flag/hidden command group (e.g., `upgrade plan` commands available but `upgrade apply` remains experimental).
- Phase B (beta): enable for 1–2 design partners (one VPC, one on-prem/air-gapped) with Solutions + SRE support present and a rollback drill.
- Phase C (GA): make plan generation the default entry point for Private upgrades; require plan validation + prechecks pass before allowing apply.

Progress updates
- 2025-03-05: Kickoff alignment with Private + Release Eng. Agreed that plan generation must be deterministic and auditable; execution will consume stored plan + stored state (rollback work to follow).
- 2025-03-19: Drafted plan schema v0 in Drive (upgrade-plan-json-schema-draft) and aligned stage names with Helm ordering proposal.
- 2025-04-02: Implemented initial plan generator (PR-4821) producing stages and validating artifact availability.
- 2025-04-11: Review feedback: add plan_hash/plan_id for traceability; make warnings vs blocking explicit in summary output; ensure offline bundle validation hooks are stubbable.
- 2025-05-07: Hooked plan generation into compatibility gating (pending platform policy wiring in installer; coordination with Quentin Harris as matrix owner).
- 2025-06-18: Remaining items for this parent ticket: finalize schema_versioning policy, wire plan summary into support bundle (ENG-4899), and align `upgrade apply` UX text with DES-311.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Plan schema versioning: do we semver the plan schema independently, or tie schema_version to Private platform minor? Proposal: schema_version independent, but enforce min installer version to read/write.
- Storage of plan/state: ConfigMap vs Secret vs local file only. Proposal: store plan in ConfigMap (non-sensitive) and store credentials/keys elsewhere; ensure support bundle can collect plan + logs.
- Offline bundle flows: should `upgrade plan` require the bundle present (on-prem) or allow generating a plan referencing a manifest URL? Proposal: on-prem requires local bundle path for verification.
- Operator contract: if prechecks are warnings, do we require explicit --ack-warnings to proceed? Proposal: yes for high-risk warnings (storage headroom, SSO reachability) with explicit acknowledgement.

Next steps
- Close out PR-4821 review items (plan_hash/plan_id, improved summary formatting, documentation strings).
- Coordinate with DES-311 to finalize CLI naming/output format.
- Ensure CI has at least one deterministic plan snapshot test + integration test stub to prevent drift (ENG-4877).
- Prepare beta checklist with Solutions/SRE and design partner scheduling (PM-826).
